notes.title: Made in Brazil Sale 2024
notes.content:
The Made in Brazil Sale is currently going on Steam. It's the 2nd consecutive year in which the event takes place, celebrating games made by Brazilian Developers!

The Made in Brazil Sale takes place between the 14th and 19th of February and has more than 500 Brazilian titles!

The sale has games already published, new releases and even titles that are yet to be released, such as Brazilian Street Food Simulator!

About the event
Conceived by Eduardo Lamhut, developer of the company Bitcake Studio from Rio de Janeiro, the action emerged after the mobilization of studios and teams from all regions of the country. A great demonstration of the growth and maturity of the national industry.

Unprecedented and officially approved by the platform, the campaign means highlighting Brazilian games in the most popular space: the Steam homepage, thus promoting consumption and the dissemination of titles.

notes.title: Made in Brazil Sale
notes.content:
The Made in Brazil Sale is currently going on Steam. It's the first event of its kind on Steam, celebrating games made by Brazilian Developers (or with Brazilians in the team), while Brazil celebrates its worldwide known Carnival event.

The Made in Brazil Sale takes place between the 18th and 23rd of February and has more than 500 titles!

The sale has games already published, new releases and even titles that are yet to be released. 

Brazilian Street Food Simulator is a highlight in the event, and I'm humbled to say that it is at the side of legendary indie games like Oniken, Celeste and others!

About the event
Conceived by Eduardo Lamhut, developer of the company Bitcake Studio from Rio de Janeiro, the action emerged after the mobilization of studios and teams from all regions of the country. A great demonstration of the growth and maturity of the national industry.

Unprecedented and officially approved by the platform, the campaign means highlighting Brazilian games in the most popular space: the Steam homepage, thus promoting consumption and the dissemination of titles.

Source from the about section: the Brazilian developer Aoca Game Lab.

notes.title: Brazilian Street Food Simulator Goes Viral In Brazil and is All Over the News
notes.content:
Brazilian Street Food Simulator was announced publicly for the first time on 19/08/22, with a Twitter post with the trailer. Just 12 hours later it reached more than 1 million impressions and more than 300,000 video views! The announcement video currently has 390K views.

A streamer with 6 million followers quickly talked about the game and a big portal that created an article about the game

After that, as of today, the game has been covered by the majority of Brazil's biggest tech and gaming websites, and by some big YouTube and Instagram accounts.

Notice that all of this happened organically, without paid advertisement and without any kind of prior contact!
